paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God knows you completely, and He hasn't backed away. David says, "O LORD, You have searched me and known me" (Psalm 139:1). He knows when David sits, when he rises, and even his thoughts from afar (Psalm 139:2). That kind of knowing could feel scary, but David isn't scared, and he calls it "too wonderful" for him (Psalm 139:6).

He isn't scared because God is with him everywhere: heaven, Sheol, the farthest sea, even the dark (Psalm 139:8-12). David says, "darkness is as light to You" (Psalm 139:12). And that closeness started before David could do a single thing, since God formed him, saw him while he was still unformed, and wrote all his days in His book before one of them came to be (Psalm 139:13, 16). So, baker, you never have to hide from Him, and you never have to earn His attention, because you had it before you took your first breath.

That's why David ends the way he does. He's already said God knows his heart, so now he ASKS Him to look: "Search me, O God, and know my heart" (Psalm 139:23). He asks God to see if there's any offensive way in him and to "lead me in the way everlasting" (Psalm 139:24). Friend, when you know you're held that tightly, you can stop hiding and start asking for help, so go ahead and say it to Him today and let Him lead.
